A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new and powerful method to study XOR games in general probabilistic theories.
we have established a new connection between the study of XOR games, tensor norms and the geometry of Banach spaces, and we have obtained new insights in all of them.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the gap between local and non-local strategies in general XOR problems is not exponentially small, as is the case in the quantum setting, but rather polynomially small, with a polynomial that can be made explicit in terms of the dimensions of the underlying Hilbert spaces.
the study of XOR games in general probabilistic theories is a fruitful approach for the study of tensor norms, which are a central object of study in functional analysis and operator algebras.
